questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Cellular Respiration and Substrates' refers to.
questions.a: The biochemical process occurring within cells where chemical bonds of organic compounds are indeed oxidised to liberate energy stored as ATP.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Cellular Respiration and Substrates'.
questions.a: Energy stored in organic nutrients is harvested through controlled enzymatic oxidation to synthesise ATP.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Cellular Respiration and Substrates', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: C6H12O6 + 6O2 -> 6CO2 + 6H2O + energy

questions.q: Calculate net ATP formed directly during glycolysis. Use the method 'Glycolysis (EMP Pathway)'. Work with: formed_atp = 100, glucose_molecules = 30, used_atp = 60. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of nadh_yield.
questions.a: 60 units

questions.q: Find the direct ATP yield in glycolytic breakdown. Use the method 'Glycolysis (EMP Pathway)'. Work with: formed_atp = 6, glucose_molecules = 400, used_atp = 18. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of nadh_yield.
questions.a: 800 units

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Glycolysis (EMP Pathway)' refers to.
questions.a: A ten-step anaerobic cytoplasmic pathway where one molecule of glucose is partially oxidised into two molecules of pyruvic acid.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Glycolysis (EMP Pathway)'.
questions.a: Glucose splits into two pyruvic acid molecules in the cytoplasm without consuming molecular oxygen.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Glycolysis (EMP Pathway)', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: net_atp = formed_atp - used_atp

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Fermentation' refers to.
questions.a: An anaerobic metabolic breakdown of pyruvate into lactic acid or ethanol and carbon dioxide with low energy release.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Fermentation'.
questions.a: Incomplete oxidation under anaerobic conditions yields metabolic byproducts and regenerates NAD+.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Fermentation', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: concept method; no single closed formula

concepts.title: Link Reaction and Tricarboxylic Acid (TCA) Cycle

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Link Reaction and Tricarboxylic Acid (TCA) Cycle' refers to.
questions.a: A mitochondrial matrix pathway where acetyl-CoA condenses with oxaloacetate to undergo cyclic decarboxylation and oxidation.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Link Reaction and Tricarboxylic Acid (TCA) Cycle'.
questions.a: Pyruvate undergoes oxidative decarboxylation to form acetyl-CoA, which fuels the cyclic generation of reduced coenzymes.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Link Reaction and Tricarboxylic Acid (TCA) Cycle', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: concept method; no single closed formula

concepts.title: Electron Transport System and Oxidative Phosphorylation

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Electron Transport System and Oxidative Phosphorylation' refers to.
questions.a: A chain of inner mitochondrial membrane protein complexes that transfer electrons to oxygen while creating a proton gradient for ATP synthesis.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Electron Transport System and Oxidative Phosphorylation'.
questions.a: Flow of electrons through respiratory complexes drives proton pumping across the inner membrane to power ATP synthase.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Electron Transport System and Oxidative Phosphorylation', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: concept method; no single closed formula

concepts.title: Respiratory Balance Sheet and ATP Calculation

questions.q: Calculate total ATP generated given counts of NADH FADH2 and direct ATP. Use the method 'Respiratory Balance Sheet and ATP Calculation'. Work with: direct_atp = 20, fadh2 = 50, nadh = 6. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of total_atp.
questions.a: 138 units

questions.q: Compute the net theoretical ATP yield from full oxidation of glucose. Use the method 'Respiratory Balance Sheet and ATP Calculation'. Work with: direct_atp = 360, fadh2 = 18, nadh = 3. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of total_atp.
questions.a: 405 units

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Respiratory Balance Sheet and ATP Calculation' refers to.
questions.a: A quantitative accounting of total theoretical ATP produced from complete oxidation of one glucose molecule.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Respiratory Balance Sheet and ATP Calculation'.
questions.a: Total theoretical yield is determined by summing direct ATP both synthesis and ATP generated from coenzyme oxidation.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Respiratory Balance Sheet and ATP Calculation', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: total_atp = (nadh * 3) + (fadh2 * 2) + direct_atp

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Amphibolic Pathway' refers to.
questions.a: A metabolic pathway that functions in both catabolic breaking-down operations and anabolic biosynthetic construction.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Amphibolic Pathway'.
questions.a: Respiratory intermediates act as precursor molecules for anabolic synthesis of lipids, proteins, and carbohydrates.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Amphibolic Pathway', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: concept method; no single closed formula

questions.q: Calculate the respiratory quotient given evolved carbon dioxide and consumed oxygen. Use the method 'Respiratory Quotient (RQ)'. Work with: volume_co2 = 360, volume_o2 = 300. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of rq.
questions.a: 1.2 units

questions.q: Find the RQ value when given volumes of CO2 evolved and O2 consumed. Use the method 'Respiratory Quotient (RQ)'. Work with: volume_co2 = 50, volume_o2 = 120. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of rq.
questions.a: 0.4167 units

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Respiratory Quotient (RQ)' refers to.
questions.a: The numerical ratio of the volume of carbon dioxide given out to the volume of oxygen taken in during respiration.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Respiratory Quotient (RQ)'.
questions.a: The ratio of CO2 produced to O2 consumed depends directly on the chemical nature of the respired substrate.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Respiratory Quotient (RQ)', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: rq = volume_co2 / volume_o2
